$comment: Single source of truth for the game's settings (hwaoi.ini next to the game). Used by the launcher's settings pages, by tools/release.py to write recomplauncher.json `settings`, and for docs/SETTINGS.md. Keys are the runtime's (runtime/cfg.c metas[]) in lower case, as the runtime writes them. `section` is the INI section the runtime files the key under (cfg.c section_of). kind: choice | toggle | slider | dynamic. `restart`: the running game only picks it up on the next start.

settings.label: Game resolution
settings.help: The size the game draws its picture in. Automatic takes your screen's size when a dedicated graphics card has the memory for it: 12 GB for 1440p, 16 GB for 4K. A size your card has too little memory for can stop the game while it loads.

settings.label: Fullscreen
settings.help: Fills the screen with a borderless window. F11 switches it while you play.

settings.label: Window size
settings.help: The size of the window when not in fullscreen.

settings.label: Frame rate
settings.help: 60 is the game's normal speed. 30 saves power.

settings.label: Screen sync
settings.help: How finished frames reach the screen. Fast shows the newest frame without tearing. V-Sync waits for the screen. Off has the least delay and can tear.

settings.label: 3D rendering
settings.help: Native draws the 3D scene at the game resolution: the sharpest picture. As on the console runs the game's own path, a 1600×900 scene scaled to 1080p: softer and lighter, and the game resolution is then 1080p.

settings.label: Upscaling
settings.help: Rebuilds the 3D picture from several frames: cleaner edges and, at a lower quality, more speed. AMD FSR works on most graphics cards and is downloaded from AMD the first time. NVIDIA DLSS needs an RTX card and NVIDIA's own DLSS file.

settings.label: DLSS quality
settings.help: DLAA keeps the full 3D resolution and only cleans the edges. Quality, Balanced and Performance draw the 3D scene smaller and scale it up: faster, a little softer.

settings.label: FSR quality
settings.help: Native keeps the full 3D resolution and only cleans the edges. Quality, Balanced and Performance draw the 3D scene smaller and scale it up: faster, a little softer.

settings.label: Frame generation
settings.help: NVIDIA DLSS draws extra frames between the game's own, so motion looks smoother on a fast screen: 4x turns 60 frames per second into 240. The game itself does not run faster, and your input is felt a little later. Needs a GeForce RTX 40 or 50 card and NVIDIA's own frame generation file. Pick a number your screen can show. While it is on, Screen sync is Off.

settings.label: Edge smoothing
settings.help: SMAA smooths jagged edges in the finished picture on any graphics card, at a small cost. With FSR or DLSS it is not needed.

settings.label: Fit to the window
settings.help: How the finished picture is scaled when the window is larger than the game resolution. AMD FSR 1 keeps edges sharper than Bilinear.

settings.label: Sharpness
settings.help: Sharpening after the picture is scaled. 0 turns it off.

settings.label: Picture shape
settings.help: The game's picture is 16:9. On a screen of another shape, keep it with black bars or stretch it over the whole window. On a 16:9 screen the two look the same.

settings.label: Performance overlay
settings.help: Frame rate and timings in a corner of the game. F10 cycles it while you play.

settings.label: Graphics card
settings.help: Which graphics card runs the game. Automatic takes a dedicated card before an integrated one.

settings.label: Device profile
settings.help: Steam Deck starts with lighter settings for handheld PCs. Automatic chooses it on a Steam Deck.

settings.label: Colour
settings.help: The game's own colours, a more vivid look, extra clarity, deeper blacks for OLED screens, or your own values below.

settings.label: Brightness
settings.help: Lighter or darker picture.

settings.label: Contrast
settings.help: Difference between light and dark.

settings.label: Saturation
settings.help: Colour strength.

settings.label: Gamma
settings.help: Mid-tone brightness.

settings.label: HDR output
settings.help: Gives an HDR screen an HDR picture, so the desktop's HDR does not dim or wash out the game. The game's picture stays the same, without extra range in the highlights. HDR has to be on for the screen in your system's settings.

settings.label: HDR peak brightness
settings.help: Your screen's peak brightness.

settings.label: HDR picture brightness
settings.help: How bright white is in the game's picture.

settings.label: HDR interface brightness
settings.help: How bright white is in the settings menu you open with Esc and in the overlay.

settings.label: Game language
settings.help: The language of the game's text and voices menu. Automatic follows your system.

settings.label: In-game menu language
settings.help: The language of the settings menu you open with Esc, and of the overlay. Automatic follows your system.

settings.label: Console mode
settings.help: Docked is the TV mode. Handheld uses the console's portable settings, lighter on slower PCs.

settings.label: Keep running in the background
settings.help: Off pauses the game when you switch to another window.

settings.label: Bonuses for other games' saves
settings.help: Tells the game you have Age of Calamity and Tears of the Kingdom saves, for their bonus items.

settings.label: Master volume
settings.help: Above 100 % boosts quiet speakers.

settings.label: Mute in the background
settings.help: Silences the game while another window is in front.

settings.label: Audio buffer
settings.help: Raise it if the sound crackles or drops out. Low reacts fastest.

settings.label: Player 1 plays with
settings.help: Automatic takes the first controller connected, with the keyboard and mouse beside it.

settings.label: Player 2 plays with
settings.help: The second player in co-op. Automatic takes the second controller; None leaves player 2 out.

settings.label: Player 1 appears to the game as
settings.help: The Switch controller the game is told this player holds, whatever the real one is. Change it only if the game asks for the other kind.

settings.label: Player 2 appears to the game as
settings.help: The Switch controller the game is told player 2 holds.

settings.label: Buttons shown in the game
settings.help: The buttons the game shows in its HUD and hints. Automatic: those of the controller you are using, with your own bindings, and the keys when you use the keyboard and mouse. Pick a maker when your controller is shown as another one, or Game's own to keep the buttons as the game draws them.

settings.label: Confirm button in menus
settings.help: The button that confirms in the game's menus; the other one goes back. Automatic: the bottom button on Xbox, PlayStation and other controllers, the right one on a Switch controller, as the game has it. Battle keeps every button, and the keyboard its keys.

settings.label: Stick dead zone
settings.help: Raise it if the camera or the character moves on its own.

settings.label: Camera speed
settings.help: How fast the right stick and the mouse turn the camera. 100 % is the game's own speed.

settings.label: Motion controls
settings.help: Uses the controller's gyro and accelerometer where the game asks for motion.

settings.label: Rumble strength
settings.help: 0 turns rumble off.

settings.label: Rumble curve
settings.help: Lower values make light rumble stronger; 1 is linear.

settings.label: Trigger rumble
settings.help: Also drives the motors in the triggers of controllers that have them.

settings.label: Mouse sensitivity
settings.help: Camera speed with the mouse.

settings.label: Prepare shaders at start
settings.help: Builds the shaders the game used before while it starts, in the background: fewer hitches in play.

settings.label: Translate effect shaders early
settings.help: Translates compute shaders as the game registers them, before an effect first needs them.

settings.label: Draw on a second thread
settings.help: Lets the game's own thread run ahead while another one draws. Can raise the frame rate when the processor is the limit, and adds one frame of delay. Experimental.

settings.label: Drawing commands on their own thread
settings.help: The game hands its drawing commands to the graphics driver on a thread of their own: more speed where a scene has many objects. Automatic turns it on, except on Radeon cards with AMD's own driver, where it has ended the game with code 70 for some players.

settings.label: Memory for the game's graphics data
settings.help: Where the game's 4.6 GB block of graphics data (vertices, constants, buffers) is kept. Video memory is much faster on a dedicated graphics card, but on Windows it also counts against the memory that RAM and the page file share. Automatic uses video memory when Windows has room for it. If the game runs at only a few frames per second on a PC with 16 GB of RAM, choose Video memory.

settings.label: Precise timer
settings.help: Asks Windows for a 1 ms timer, so the game's short waits do not last a whole 15 ms tick.

settings.label: Memory on demand
settings.help: Windows: takes game memory as it is first used. About 2 GB less is reserved, with more small hitches while loading. Automatic turns it on only when the PC could not give the game all its memory otherwise.

settings.label: Smaller video memory blocks
settings.help: Takes video memory 128 MB at a time instead of 256: less is held unused.

settings.label: Compress shader sources
settings.help: Keeps the game's shader programs compressed in memory.

settings.label: Texture decoding
settings.help: Where the game's ASTC textures are decoded. Automatic: by the graphics card itself where it can read them, else by a compute shader on it, else on the processor.

settings.label: Video memory limit for kept textures
settings.help: Above this share of video memory in use, textures the game has released are dropped instead of being kept for reuse.

settings.label: Thread hand-over
settings.help: How a waiting game thread gets a processor core from the one holding it. Full interrupts the holder, Light only passes its priority on, Off waits. For bug reports.

settings.label: No limit of one thread per console core
settings.help: The console runs one game thread per core, and the game is timed for that. On lets its threads run on any core at once. For bug reports: it can break the game's timing.

settings.label: Vulkan validation
settings.help: For bug reports only: much slower. Needs the Vulkan SDK.

settings.label: Flight recorder
settings.help: Records timing spikes into the log for bug reports.

settings.label: Draw call markers
settings.help: For bug reports about a graphics card that stops answering (code 70): the log then names the draw calls it was working on. A little slower.
